findings.title: Procurements were not always made in accordance with established policies or applicable State law.
findings.description: BCPS obtained program evaluation services using a contract from an Illinois school system that did not qualify as an intergovernmental cooperative purchasing agreement (ICPA) and was not competitively procured. BCPS also failed to document evaluations for instructional material procurements totaling $1.5 million and did not publish four contract awards totaling $23.7 million on eMaryland Marketplace as required by State law.

dollar_amounts.context: four contract awards not published on eMaryland Marketplace
instructional materials procurements lacking documentation of evaluations
program evaluation services paid using non-ICPA contract

findings.recommendation: BCPS should comply with established policies and State law by discontinuing procurement from contracts without provisions for use by other entities or not competitively procured, documenting evaluations of potential vendors for instructional materials, and publishing ICPA contract awards greater than $50,000 in eMMA.

findings.title: BCPS’ written policy did not define the criteria for what constitutes a contract modification and did not require a signed contract modification to support changes to contract terms and conditions.
findings.description: BCPS executed significant changes to contracts without written modifications or Board approval. This included $1.9 million in expenditures during an extended contract period without a formal agreement, and $1.2 million paid for upgraded antitheft devices on a computer lease contract without modifying the contract terms.

dollar_amounts.context: expenditures made during extended contract period without written modification
upgraded antitheft devices paid for without modifying contract terms

findings.recommendation: BCPS should amend its written policy to establish criteria for contract modifications and require a signed contract modification for significant changes. BCPS should also present contract modifications to the Board for review and approval as required.

findings.title: BCPS did not use an ICPA for purchasing school buses in a manner intended and limited competition for those procurements. BCPS also did not maintain supporting documentation to enable us to determine whether it received the best value.
findings.description: BCPS purchased 197 school buses totaling $19.5 million using an ICPA but did not use the pricing in the agreement or document the rationale for not doing so. BCPS awarded a bus order to the vendor with the highest price, exceeding the lowest bidder's total by approximately $139,000.

dollar_amounts.context: school buses purchased under ICPA without using pricing or documentation
price difference between highest bidder and lowest bidder for bus purchase

findings.recommendation: BCPS should adhere to ICPA terms and conditions including pricing, document justification of material changes to procurement methods, and notify the Board of material changes.

findings.title: BCPS did not have a written policy requiring the documentation of the receipt of goods and services prior to making the related payment and permitted the prepayment of vendors for services without a formal policy. Further, BCPS did not ensure that contracts were always properly executed prior to payment.
findings.description: Seven payments totaling $1.3 million lacked documentation that goods or services were received prior to approval. BCPS prepaid one vendor $636,000 without verifying services were provided and paid a vendor $270,000 before the contract was finalized.

dollar_amounts.context: payments lacking documentation of receipt of goods or services
prepayment to vendor for professional development without verification
payment made before contract was finalized

findings.recommendation: BCPS should develop written policies requiring formal documentation of receipt of goods and services prior to payment. BCPS should also ensure contracts are properly executed prior to receiving services or making payments.

findings.title: BCPS did not ensure certain personnel and payroll transactions processed were subject to independent review and approval, resulting in overpayments to six employees totaling $70,839 going undetected.
findings.description: System reports of payroll transactions were initially received by the employee processing them before independent review. Testing identified 6 overpayments totaling $70,839 that went undetected during supervisory review. Additionally, time entered into the electronic system was not always approved by immediate supervisors for thousands of employees.

dollar_amounts.context: overpayments to six employees going undetected

findings.recommendation: BCPS should perform comprehensive independent reviews of all critical personnel and payroll transactions, review payroll transactions for potential overpayments and pursue recovery, and ensure appropriate supervisory approval of electronic time records.

findings.title: BCPS did not ensure that employee access to its automated financial systems was appropriate and adequately controlled, resulting in employees with unnecessary or incompatible access.
findings.description: Testing disclosed employees had the ability to process purchase orders without independent approval. Additionally, 128 employees initiated and approved requisitions for $1.1 million without any independent review during the tested period.

dollar_amounts.context: purchase orders initiated and approved without independent review

findings.recommendation: BCPS should periodically review employee access capabilities to ensure all access is appropriate and incompatible duties are segregated. BCPS should also correct any unnecessary or improper capabilities.

findings.title: Sensitive BCPS personally identifiable information was maintained in a manner that did not provide adequate security safeguards.
findings.description: A significant computer application containing sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) existed without adequate security safeguards. As of October 2019, the database contained over 92,000 unique sensitive records vulnerable to improper disclosure.
findings.recommendation: BCPS should implement appropriate information security safeguards for its sensitive PII.

findings.title: For two critical systems’ databases, security and audit event logging and monitoring procedures were not adequate, and unnecessary elevated system privileges were granted to numerous user accounts.
findings.description: Two critical systems' database configurations did not include logging of eight categories of critical security events. Improper database roles granting highest administrative privilege levels were assigned to 34 user accounts over the respective databases.
findings.recommendation: BCPS should implement appropriate database monitoring controls including logging all significant activities, ensuring regular independent reviews of reports, and restricting assignment of critical database administration roles.

findings.title: Twenty-six publicly accessible servers were improperly located within the internal network, intrusion detection prevention system coverage for untrusted traffic did not exist, and BCPS network resources were not secured against improper access from students using wireless connections and high school computer labs.
findings.description: Publicly accessible servers were located in the internal network rather than a protected zone. Intrusion detection prevention system (IDPS) coverage did not exist for untrusted encrypted traffic. Student network-level access was not adequately filtered to limit administrative server access.
findings.recommendation: BCPS should relocate publicly accessible servers to a separate protected network zone, assess and implement IDPS coverage for untrusted traffic, and limit student network-level access.

findings.title: BCPS did not use its automated bus routing software to periodically perform a system-wide analysis of routes and related bus capacities to maximize efficiency and had not established comprehensive bus routing procedures.
findings.description: BCPS had not used its automated bus routing software for a system-wide analysis. Review of 552 morning bus routes disclosed that 183 routes were designed to transport students at less than 75 percent of customary capacity goals, with some under 50 percent.
findings.recommendation: BCPS should use automated bus routing software to periodically perform a system-wide analysis of bus routes and establish comprehensive bus routing procedures specifying target capacities and ridership goals.

findings.title: Claims payments totaling approximately $152.2 million during fiscal year 2019 were not reviewed for propriety.
findings.description: Claim payments for employee health care costs totaled approximately $152.2 million in fiscal year 2019 but were not independently reviewed to ensure billed services were provided or covered by self-insured plans. Neither BCPS nor the County conducted independent audits of paid claims.

dollar_amounts.context: claims payments for employee health care costs not reviewed for propriety

findings.recommendation: BCPS should work with the County to ensure paid claims are reasonable by independently verifying or contracting for periodic independent audits.

extraction.agency_response_summary: BCPS generally agreed with all findings and recommendations. The agency provided specific corrective action plans for each recommendation, including policy revisions, system upgrades, and procedural changes, with estimated completion dates ranging from September 2020 to June 2022.
extraction.extraction_notes: Audit period derived from methodology section (July 1, 2015 to April 30, 2019). Prior findings count based on preceding report table listing 12 findings. Dollar amounts converted to integers.
